title: Make the throughput review measure wasted work, not only landed time
summary: Add attempts per landed change, spend on attempts that did not land, and first-attempt share to the throughput section (newest 20 landings vs the 20 before). Hestia's throughput review triggers on a rise in any of them, notes rather than skips on an open design request, and queues a request only when the change exceeds recent-window noise. Audience: the maintainer reading `athena status` and the review.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for each behavior; cargo test and clippy pass.
Criteria run tests asserting values 2.0 and 0.5, triggers and no-skip.
Status output exercised via test or cargo run.
One focused change to the review, status and record.
Checks that wasted work is seen and triggers the review.
Doc comments and CHANGELOG written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs: `throughput_due(landed, median, latest)` (~line 1341) is the trigger, called from the throughput review in `Athena::review_passes` (~line 1711); right after it, `open_throughput_request` (~line 1728) currently stops the review when a design request is open, so the order is: trigger check, then the open-request skip, then the model proposal, then slowdown/stage growth. Read crates/athena-core/src/status.rs: `Throughput::compute(&Records)` (~line 984) builds the section over `THROUGHPUT_WINDOW` = 20 newest landed jobs, already tracks `unlanded_jobs`/`unlanded_minutes`, and `Throughput::text()` is what `athena status` prints via crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs. The new measures are computed directly from job/attempt records and outcome totals (cost) in `Throughput::compute`, not through the minutes stand-in. Read crates/athena-data/src/records.rs: `ThroughputReview` (~line 2188) and `ThroughputTrigger` (Cadence, Worsened) are accepted by `AnyRecord::parse` / `check_record_file` (line 3111) via `AnyRecord::ThroughputReview(r) => r.validate()`; the change adds fields with serde defaults (so old records still parse) and new trigger variants, and is covered by `ThroughputReview::validate` plus a round-trip test through `AnyRecord::parse` in records.rs tests. No new record file type or allow-list entry is added.
Prior-window comparison reuses the previous review's stored measures (new defaulted fields on ThroughputReview) or recomputes the 20-before window from records; the producer picks the simpler one.

Noise is estimated as the spread (e.g. max-min or median absolute deviation) of the measure across recent 20-landing windows; a request is queued only when the change exceeds it, and the review note says whether it did.
Wasted spend = cost of attempts on jobs/attempts that did not land, from outcome totals; first-attempt share = landed changes with exactly one attempt / landed changes.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new status.rs test builds sample records where half of attempts in the window did not land and asserts attempts per landing == 2.0 and first-attempt share == 0.5.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new hestia.rs test shows `throughput_due` (or its successor) returns a trigger when wasted spend rises beyond the previous review and noise while median minutes is unchanged; the same inputs without the rise return None.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a new hestia.rs test shows an open earlier design request no longer stops the review: the review runs, and its record note mentions the open request.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test shows a change within the noise between recent windows queues no request and the note says it was within noise, while a larger change queues one.

Run `cargo test -p athena-cli` and `cargo run -- status` (or the status_snapshot test): the throughput output shows attempts per landed change, money spent on attempts that did not land, and first-attempt share.
Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass; an old ThroughputReview JSON without the new fields still parses via `AnyRecord::parse`, and a new one round-trips.
CHANGELOG.md has entries naming only what the diff does (the three measures, new triggers, open-request note, noise rule); no unrelated claims.
The doc comment of hestia.rs and the Throughput review section of docs/design/hestia.md no longer say an open design request skips the review (Grep for the old wording finds none).

out_of_scope: Changing the slowdown request's 25% rule or the stage-growth comparison beyond what the noise rule needs.
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows or prompt files.
departures: Larger than typical: touches trigger logic, the stored review record and status display, so cost and time are above the reference and verification is somewhat less likely.
hard_reason: Changes the rule that triggers, holds or queues Hestia's throughput review (the open-request skip and a new noise threshold) and the review record it stores.
